sections.title: In brief
sections.text: This collection examines digital processes in architecture, spanning design generation, fabrication and buildings that sense or respond to their surroundings.

sections.title: Organizing question
sections.text: How do digital tools change architecture both as ways of conceiving and constructing form and as means of operating interactive environments?

sections.title: Editorial premise
sections.text: The introduction links a move beyond standardized production with complex customized forms. It also treats data about environmental behavior and content as relevant to architectural design.

sections.title: How the issue is organized
sections.text: An opening Bier–Knight editorial is followed by five independently authored contributions. The issue combines historical, conceptual and design-project perspectives; those methods must be checked article by article.

sections.title: Useful reading examples
sections.text: Fox discusses interactive-environment history; Rosenberg addresses transformable scissor-pair structures; Gullström examines framing and transparency in mediated windows. These are separate investigations, not examples tested by one common protocol.

sections.title: What can be concluded here
sections.text: The collection connects digital generation and fabrication with sensing and actuation. The issue introduction establishes a research agenda, not proof that these systems improve every building.

sections.title: Limits and dates
sections.text: Spring 2010 is the issue designation. The platform displays a 2014 posting date. This guide summarizes the editors’ framing and contents, not the results of every paper.

sections.title: Why browse it
sections.text: It broadens a grammar-focused perspective: generating geometry is one part of a larger design–fabrication–interaction process.
